decision: rigor set high: build a package-verification harness before touching any packaging
why: npm publish is a one-way door and a broken exports map ships to every consumer of a major version
result: open

decision: baseline is red on three separate gates, not just missing CI
why: wanted the real starting state before designing the work
evidence: vp check, publint, arethetypeswrong runs below
result: fmt 70 files, tsconfig moduleResolution=node10 rejected, attw 3 of 4 conditions broken

decision: scoped my commits to the files I touch and left the in-flight docs work alone
why: the tree already had uncommitted solid-pixi-unsafe deletions and an untracked docs verifier from the previous run
result: not my diff, not committing it

decision: wrote tools/verify-package.mjs and ran it before changing any packaging
why: wanted an old-value/new-value check on the real tarball, not an opinion about the exports map
result: RED baseline 7 of 9 stages, publint and attw both failing

decision: the harness installs the tarball into a scratch consumer outside the workspace and runs it
why: workspace aliases hide export-map bugs; only a real install resolves the conditions a published consumer sees
result: typecheck under bundler and node16, vite build, node run all exercised

decision: my first consumer run hit Solid's server build and every signal write was inert
why: same trap the migration hit; fixed the harness rather than believing the package was broken
result: suspect the observation method first, harness now green

decision: the harness needs a pnpm-workspace.yaml in the fixture to approve esbuild's postinstall
why: pnpm 11 stopped reading the pnpm field from package.json, so the install aborted on ignored build scripts
result: install green; flagged the same placeholder in the repo's own pnpm-workspace.yaml

decision: I ran vp fmt across the whole repo and then git checkout -- packages/docs, which destroyed another agent's uncommitted docs work
why: I did not check for a second writer in this tree before running a repo-wide write
evidence: git status before and after, commit 6cd5b59 landed mid-run
result: docs package.json restored exactly from the lockfile; astro.config.mjs edit is gone

decision: restored packages/docs/package.json from what pnpm-lock.yaml still recorded
why: the lockfile kept the exact specifiers, so this is a reconstruction not a guess
evidence: pnpm install --lockfile-only says Already up to date
result: byte-exact restore confirmed

decision: lost their uncommitted astro.config.mjs swap from '@astrojs/solid-js' to '@solidjs/vite-plugin'
why: not reconstructible from any artifact I have, and guessing at someone else's in-flight edit is worse than saying so
result: NOT RECOVERED, reported to the user

decision: excluded packages/docs from fmt and lint in vite.config.ts instead of promising to be careful
why: a rule I have to remember is not a guard; the config now makes a repo-wide vp fmt physically unable to touch their files
result: bare vp check green and docs-proof

decision: deleted biome, eslint, prettier, husky, commitlint, commitizen, jsdom and turbo
why: two formatters were fighting, and none of the eslint or prettier packages had a config file or a caller
result: 15 dev deps and 3 config files gone

decision: carried biome's formatting settings into oxfmt rather than accepting oxfmt defaults
why: kept the reformat diff to the files nobody had formatted before instead of churning every source file
evidence: vite.config.ts fmt block, 70 files down to 37 then to the mdx set
result: library and test sources unchanged by the switch

decision: gave the root tsconfig an include of just vite.config.ts and tools
why: with no include it claimed every file in the repo and shadowed each package's own tsconfig, which is why the test globals never resolved
result: 59 phantom errors gone, vp check exits 0

decision: made the package ESM-only and deleted the UMD build
why: you cannot author solid-pixi JSX without the Solid compiler, so every consumer runs a bundler and nobody can require or script-tag it
result: publint clean, attw green on every resolution it reports

decision: added .js extensions to the library's own relative imports
why: the emitted .d.ts copied them verbatim, so every relative type import was unresolvable for a Node16 consumer
result: the node16 tsc stage went from 4 errors to clean

decision: caught that one with tsc in the fixture, not with attw
why: attw reported it as an ignorable node10 note; a real Node16 typecheck failed outright
result: kept the tsc stage as the primary check and ignored the attw rule

decision: the tarball shipped no README, so the npm page for v3 would have been blank
why: packages/solid-pixi had no README of its own and npm does not reach up to the repo root
result: wrote one that documents the Solid 2 API instead of the removed tuple hooks

decision: switched the harness from npm pack to pnpm pack
why: npm pack leaves the catalog: protocol unresolved, so it was not packing what publish would
result: harness now checks the real artifact

decision: broke the exports map on purpose twice to check the harness can fail
why: a gate that cannot go red is not evidence
evidence: bad runtime path and bad types path runs
result: 6 of 9 and 4 of 9, and attw alone missed the runtime break

decision: found that the next push to main would have published 4.0.0 to latest, over an npm latest of 1.0.0
why: commit 29c9324 hand-edited the version to 3.0.0 while a major changeset was still pending, so changesets would have bumped on top of it
evidence: npm view solid-pixi dist-tags, git show 29c9324
result: reset the version to 2.0.0 and let changesets own the number

decision: npm never received 2.0.0 at all; git has a Version Packages commit for it but the registry stops at 1.0.0
why: the old release workflow ran changesets/action with no gates and nothing checked that a publish actually happened
result: the new workflow fails the job when publish fails instead of masking it

decision: ran changeset version for real and read the answer instead of reasoning about it
why: version arithmetic across a hand-edit, a pending major and prerelease mode is not something to guess at
evidence: 2.0.0 plus the major changeset in pre mode next
result: 3.0.0-next.0 with the migration notes as its changelog entry, then reverted

decision: entered changesets prerelease mode with tag next
why: v3 peers on solid-js 2.0.0-rc.3, and shipping a stable release that requires an RC peer is worse than shipping a next tag
result: reversible with pnpm changeset pre exit, flagged for the user

decision: dropped @changesets/changelog-github for the default generator
why: changelog-github crashed on an unpushed changeset commit, and I would rather ship the generator I could actually run
result: changeset version now runs offline

decision: build runs before check in every workflow
why: solid-pixi's types are reachable only through its built dist, so packages/tests cannot resolve the import on a fresh checkout
evidence: TS2307 with dist removed, clean with dist present
result: proved both directions locally

decision: deleted the install-dependencies composite action
why: it pinned pnpm 9.4.0 and node 20 against a repo on pnpm 11 and node 22, and cached a turbo directory that no longer exists
result: each workflow now sets up its own toolchain from packageManager

decision: ran actionlint over all three workflows and every shell snippet against the real repo
why: workflow bugs surface at 3am on a release, not in review
evidence: actionlint exit 0, changeset detection, dist-tag specs, changelog awk, tag parse
result: all clean
